dataset.name: WANDS's real product.csv (a preregistered 36-key sample) plus automotive's real 17-field native attribute set; end-to-end scoring uses WANDS's real 480 queries and 233,448 real relevance judgments

engine_config.statistics_only: issue42_eval::e2b_statistics_baseline::classify (no access to a field's own name)
engine_config.llm_no_validator: frozen subagent JSON output, first-run-wins per real key, evaluation only
engine_config.note: no production commerce_core code was touched by E2b's own implementation

repetitions: 8 independent frozen LLM-proposal artifacts (4 perturbation configurations x 2 runs each); repeated-run agreement (role + physical primitive) measured directly: 107/125 (85.60%)

headline_result.baseline_1_statistics_only: macro F1=0.5366, accepted-structural precision=0.9783 recall=1.0000 (n_accepted=46), abstention_rate=0.0000 -- the honest 'no semantic understanding' floor.
headline_result.baseline_2_llm_no_validator: macro F1=0.6050, accepted-structural precision=0.9778 recall=0.9778 (n_accepted=45), abstention_rate=0.0189.
headline_result.baseline_3_llm_plus_validator: macro F1=0.6269, accepted-structural precision=0.9756 recall=0.8889 (n_accepted=41), abstention_rate=0.1321.
headline_result.repeated_run_agreement: 107/125 (85.60%) role+primitive agreement across all 4 configurations. Concrete real disagreement: automotive's thread_size classified enum/bitmap_enum by run 1, numeric/numeric_range by run 2.
headline_result.macro_f1_by_configuration: wands_baseline=0.6753 (best, real key visible), wands_noisy=0.6573 (close to baseline -- misleading names did not meaningfully fool the proposing passes), wands_anonymized=0.4900 (clearest real degradation -- losing the key's own name costs real accuracy), automotive=0.2597 (smaller 17-field sample makes each miss proportionally costlier).
headline_result.end_to_end: oracle NDCG@10=0.0100 Recall@10=0.0004 (n_queries_scored=270), statistics-only identical to oracle, LLM+validator NDCG@10=0.0108 Recall@10=0.0004 (n_queries_scored=251) -- relative NDCG gap vs oracle 7.57%. This naive, unranked, substring-matched end-to-end check produces near-floor NDCG for every baseline including oracle and is flagged unreliable at this magnitude by the binary itself (e2e_check_reliable=false), disclosed rather than treated as a clean pass or fail.
headline_result.go_gate: zero unsafe accepted (0 found) -- PASS; >=80% recall on retrieval-significant reference features (100.0%) -- PASS; end-to-end relevance within 5% of oracle (relative gap 7.57%, check itself unreliable) -- INCONCLUSIVE; >=90% repeated-run agreement (85.60%) -- FAIL; real structured unseen feed evidence (WANDS) -- PASS.
headline_result.verdict: REVISE, not GO, not STOP. Two gates pass cleanly, one fails outright (stability, a real if modest shortfall), one is inconclusive because the end-to-end check's own naive design cannot produce a trustworthy signal at this magnitude -- recorded as inconclusive per Issue #42 rule 12, not manufactured into a pass or fail. Directionally encouraging but does not clear the preregistered bar as stated. E4/E5/E6 remain explicitly out of scope (protocol/design only) per Issue #42's own scope boundary.

confirmed_defects_found_and_fixed.defect: unsafe_accepted_count incremented on every validator *rejection* (!validation.accepted), measuring the opposite of 'unsafe accepted structural classification' -- a rejection is the validator working correctly, not an unsafe acceptance.
confirmed_defects_found_and_fixed.fix: Redefined against the protocol's own wording: an accepted (non-abstain, structural) descriptor in the final validated set whose oracle-confirmed real role is actually Identifier or Relationship. Extracted into a standalone, unit-tested unsafe_accepted_count function.

confirmed_defects_found_and_fixed.defect: e2b_ingest::build_catalog matched the real CSV feature key against a descriptor's raw `.key` field, never `.real_key` -- correct for oracle/statistics-only (whose key is always the true feed column) but wrong for the LLM+validator baseline, since WANDS's alphabetically-first config (wands_anonymized) always won the per-real-key first-resolved race, leaving every accepted WANDS field looking for a CSV column (e.g. 'feature_5') that does not exist.
confirmed_defects_found_and_fixed.fix: Added real_key_of(d) -> d.real_key.as_deref().unwrap_or(&d.key) and used it everywhere build_catalog keys its typed_keys/typed_by_key maps.
confirmed_defects_found_and_fixed.post_correction_value: LLM + validator: NDCG@10=0.0108 Recall@10=0.0004 (n_queries_scored=251), directly comparable to oracle's own NDCG@10=0.0100 (n_queries_scored=270)

note: Both defects were found by adversarial self-review before any number was trusted (Issue #42's own 'do not trust the experiment author' governance), were entirely within the evaluation harness (crates/issue42-eval), and involved zero changes to commerce_core or to any preregistered GO-gate threshold. Both pre- and post-correction numbers are preserved in docs/research/artifacts/i42_e2b_run1/ per rule 9 (never silently replace an invalidated number).
